newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Sket expects to pay back state aid.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Sket expects to pay back state aid.

text.p: Ailing east German heavy machinery firm Sket expects to have to pay back at least 1.2 billion marks ($707.6 million) in state aid, a spokesman for the firm said on Tuesday.

He added that the final figure will depend on the result of an enquiry into the matter due to be launched by European Commission competition authorities in Brussels on Wednesday. He stressed that the six newly-created Sket businesses set up as part of a rescue plan would not be affected.
Sket received aid from the BvS, the successor to Germany's Treuhand privatisation agency, during 1995 and 1996. That aid was however dependent on EC approval.

In March, the BvS approved a rescue plan for Sket which included cutting a three-quarters of its jobs. The firm, once a main supplier to communist eastern Europe, has received over a billion marks in state aid since unification.
